Context: Cal and Marie Callender married in 1924. After spending 20 years raising their son Don, Marie decided to start a career in cooking.
Title: [Excerpt from] Marie Callender: Homemade Pie Maven
Author: by Rebecca Felix
Content: Callender had become a skilled baker and cook while taking care of her family. In the 1940s, she decided to put these skills to work outside the home. Callender took a part-time job at a delicatessen. There, she made salads and hot foods.
:box:delicatessen = store where you can buy food that is already made, such as a sandwich

Soon, the delicatessen's owner asked Callender to make pies. She baked the pies at home, using her own recipes. Then she brought the pies to the delicatessen. Customers loved the pies' light, flaky crusts and fresh fruit or cream fillings. The desserts were soon very popular...

The demand for Callender's pies continued to grow. Soon, she could not keep up on her own. Callender spoke with her son and husband about helping her. The Callenders decided to turn making pies into a family business.

Callender also spoke with her boss about how busy she had become baking pies. He supported her decision to quit her job to focus on making pies full time. And he promised to buy pies from her for his restaurant. He even let Callender take the oven from his bakery to use in her new business.

With the oven and help from Cal and Don, Callender was ready to get to work. She planned to sell hundreds of pies to local restaurants each week. But making that many pies would require a bigger space than the Callenders' home kitchen.
The Callenders sold the family car. They used the money to fund the business. They rented a Quonset hut in Long Beach, California. The family also purchased baking equipment and supplies...
:box:Quonset hut = metal building originally used by the military that can be turned into a kitchen or office

The Callenders' success continued for the next 16 years. By then, they were baking thousands of pies each week. They made enough profit to buy better equipment. This included a commercial mixer that could mix the ingredients for many pies at once. The family also bought a new truck for delivering the pies to stores.
